incidents.vector: Mass password-spraying and SSL VPN hash interception against internet-exposed Fortinet (and MSSQL) devices, with stolen configuration files cracked offline on a 45-GPU cluster to recover plaintext admin and VPN credentials.
incidents.impact: Valid administrative and VPN credentials for roughly 73,932 FortiGate firewalls across 194 countries were exposed; confirmed compromises include a Turkish NATO defense contractor from which classified documents were allegedly exfiltrated.

incidents.vector: SocGholish/FakeUpdates malware delivered via fake browser-update prompts on compromised WordPress sites, used as an initial-access botnet feeding ransomware and espionage operations.
incidents.impact: An international law enforcement operation (US, Canada, Germany, Netherlands, Europol) seized 106 servers and disinfected nearly 15,000 infected sites, disrupting the Evil Corp-linked SocGholish initial-access botnet active since 2017.

incidents.victim: Higher-education institutions & large enterprises (Univ. of Nottingham, Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar)
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-35273) before the June 10 patch, deploying disguised MeshCentral agents and a lateral-movement/defacement script to steal data.
incidents.impact: Over 100 organizations were notified (68% higher education); stolen data has been published on the group's leak site and victims extorted, including 450,000+ University of Nottingham records and the Council of Europe (alleged 297GB).

incidents.victim: Salesforce customers via Klue Battlecards (Huntress, Recorded Future)
incidents.vector: Compromise of Klue's third-party integration backend (via a long-dormant but active test credential) and theft of customer OAuth tokens, used to query and bulk-exfiltrate connected Salesforce instances through the REST API.
incidents.impact: Salesforce suspended the Battlecards integration after attackers exfiltrated business contacts, price quotes and sales data from multiple customers; the emerging Icarus extortion group is demanding ransoms. Continues the Salesloft Drift/Gainsight OAuth-abuse pattern.

incidents.vector: Initial access via an exposed high-privilege GitHub personal access token in client-side JavaScript on an obscure subdomain, used to clone private repositories and harvest further credentials for deeper network pivoting.
incidents.impact: Threat group FulcrumSec claims it spent two months inside and exfiltrated ~1.3TB (700,000+ files) including source code, drug research, internal AI models and clinical-trial data, demanded $25M, and began leaking after non-payment; a second group also claimed an intrusion.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion disrupting IT and milling operations, paired with data theft for double extortion.
incidents.impact: Two Queensland sugar mills (Racecourse and Farleigh) have been shut since June 10 at the start of the cane-crushing season; the Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service group claims data theft and threatens to leak it absent payment.

incidents.vector: Client-side-only authorization in FIFA's Microsoft Entra tenant let a self-registered 'football agent' account reach backend APIs that performed no server-side access enforcement.
incidents.impact: An ethical hacker gained control of World Cup live TV-stream production, match-management, commentary and analytics systems; the flaw was reported via CISA/FBI and fixed the next day, with no known malicious exploitation.

incidents.victim: Mastra npm ecosystem users (developers, CI/CD pipelines)
incidents.vector: Takeover of the 'ehindero' npm maintainer account to publish 140+ poisoned @mastra packages injecting 'easy-day-js', a dayjs typosquat whose postinstall hook ran an obfuscated dropper that disabled TLS checks and fetched a second-stage tasking implant.
incidents.impact: Any workstation or pipeline running npm install of the compromised versions risked theft of credentials, tokens and build secrets plus persistent remote access; npm removed the packages and revoked the attacker's publish access.

incidents.vector: Malicious LiteLLM versions (1.82.7/1.82.8) published to PyPI using valid publishing access, embedding code to steal cloud credentials, API keys and crypto wallets and to install a persistent downloader for follow-on intrusions.
incidents.impact: LiteLLM sees ~3M daily downloads and is present in an estimated 36% of cloud environments; exposed credentials should be treated as compromised. Part of TeamPCP's broader 1,000+ package open-source supply chain campaign.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploitation of externally facing REDCap research servers with custom INFINITERED malware to harvest credentials, then pivoting to internal networks and abusing Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward matched emails.
incidents.impact: Undetected for over a year (initial compromise Sept 2023, activity through Nov 2025), the China-nexus actor pursued AI, cyber, medical and national-defense research; Google disrupted the infrastructure and notified affected organizations.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply chain compromise (Mini Shai-Hulud worm)
incidents.vector: A compromised GitHub account was used to push credential-stealing 'Miasma' malware — a cosmetically reskinned variant of the self-propagating Mini Shai-Hulud worm — into Red Hat's software pipeline.
incidents.impact: 32 packages downloaded roughly 117,000 times per week were tainted before Red Hat pulled them; the open-sourcing of the worm by TeamPCP has spawned copycat activity, complicating attribution.

incidents.victim: Four major Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, Export Development Bank)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack reportedly targeting communications infrastructure shared by the four banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for the four banks were down over a weekend; the country's banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused the AUR 'adopt' mechanism to take over 1,900+ orphaned community packages and modified their install procedures to pull a malicious npm (later Bun) script delivering a rootkit and an infostealer.
incidents.impact: Hijacked packages installed a rootkit plus credential- and developer-secret-stealing malware; affected users were urged to rotate all passwords and tokens. Hijacking attempts remained ongoing during the response.

incidents.victim: 1.2M+ WordPress sites (OptinMonster, TrustPulse, PushEngage plugin users)
incidents.vector: Malicious code added to the legitimate JavaScript of three Awesome Motive WordPress plugins; it waits for an admin login, creates a rogue admin account, then installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin to maintain access.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million sites were backdoored via the compromised plugins, granting attackers persistent administrative control; remediation across affected sites is ongoing.

incidents.victim: US security clearance holders / current & former government employees
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese intelligence created 13 fake 'consulting' company websites with AI-generated personas and job postings to recruit clearance holders and pay (via crypto) for insider and classified information.
incidents.impact: DOJ and the FBI seized the 13 domains used to lure Americans into disclosing sensitive U.S. government information through sham consulting contracts and confidentiality agreements.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257), including via a public proof-of-concept, to initiate unauthorized VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed widespread probing and a small number of successful gateway-connected sessions, with no post-access lateral movement confirmed yet. The CVE was added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29.
